title: 6.2 Bisectors of Triangles

icans: I can use the Circumcenter Theorem to find distances to the vertices.
I can find the circumcenter of a triangle in the coordinate plane.
I can use the Incenter Theorem to find distances to the sides.

vocab: three or more lines, rays, or segments that ____________ in the same point
the point where concurrent lines, rays, or segments ____________
the point of concurrency of the ________________ bisectors of a triangle
the point of ______________ of the angle bisectors of a triangle

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Circumcenter Theorem: the circumcenter of a triangle is equidistant from the _______________ of the triangle.

blocks.stem: Point P is the circumcenter of △ABC. PA = 3x + 2 and PB = 5x − 8. Find x and PC.

notes: Where the circumcenter is: inside an acute triangle, at the midpoint of the hypotenuse of a right triangle, and _______________ an obtuse triangle.

blocks.stem: Find the circumcenter of the triangle with vertices A(−1, 4), B(−1, −2), and C(5, −2).

notes: Incenter Theorem: the incenter of a triangle is equidistant from the _______________ of the triangle, and it is always inside.
Which point? The same distance from three points: the circumcenter. The same distance from three lines or sides: the _______________.

blocks.stem: Point N is the incenter of △ABC. D, E, and F are where the perpendicular segments from N meet the sides. ND = 2x − 1 and NE = x + 4. Find x and NF.
The angle bisectors of △ABC meet at P. Point K is on A̅B̅ with P̅K̅ ⊥ A̅B̅. PA = 10 and AK = 8. Find the distance from P to B̅C̅.

tickets.stem: Which point of concurrency is the same distance from all three vertices of a triangle?
Is the circumcenter of an obtuse triangle inside, on, or outside the triangle?
